text.title: Search form removed with no replacement
text.problem: The change deletes the form and input that let users enter a search term. The page now asks users to type a term but offers no input.
text.consequence: Users who open the search page without q have no way to search.
text.fix: Keep the search form on the page, both in the empty state and above the results.

truth.text: useState and useEffect are called after an early return, so the number of hooks changes when the query appears or disappears, which React rejects with an error. The fix is to call every hook before the early return.

text.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
text.problem: The heading puts the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping. The query text therefore reaches the DOM as live HTML.
text.consequence: An attacker can send a link such as /search?q= to run script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
text.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so that React escapes it.

truth.text: The search term from the URL is put into the page as HTML, so a link with a script in q runs that script for whoever opens it (cross-site scripting). The fix is to render the text as a child, {`Results for ${query}`}, which React escapes.

text.title: Any user can delete any account
text.problem: The change exempts destroy from require_admin on line 2. The destroy action then deletes any user found by params[:id].
text.consequence: Any authenticated non-admin can delete every account, including admin accounts.
text.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exception list. Alternatively, restrict destroy to the current user's own record.

evidence.context:
def show
     render json: User.find(params[:id]).as_json(only: [:id, :email])
   end
+
+  def update
+    user = User.find(params[:id])
+    user.update!(params.require(:user).permit!)
+    render json: user.as_json(only: [:id, :email])
+  end
+
+  def destroy
+    User.find(params[:id]).destroy!
+    head :no_content
+  end
 end

text.title: Any user can delete any user
text.problem: The change exempts destroy from require_admin on line 2. The destroy action then deletes any User by id with no ownership check.
text.consequence: Any authenticated non-admin can delete every account, including admin accounts.
text.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exemption list. Alternatively, scope the lookup to the current user.

text.title: Upload name allows path traversal
text.problem: make_thumbnail joins upload_name from the form into the input and output paths without validation. A name containing ../ escapes UPLOAD_DIR and THUMB_DIR.
text.consequence: An uploader can make convert read files outside the upload folder. The uploader can also overwrite files outside the thumbnail folder.
text.fix: Reduce upload_name to its basename with os.path.basename. Reject names that differ or start with a dash.

evidence.context:
@@ -0,0 +1,9 @@
+import subprocess
+
+from tools.settings import THUMB_DIR, UPLOAD_DIR
+
+
+def make_thumbnail(upload_name: str) -> None:
+    """Writes a 128 pixel thumbnail of an uploaded image. The name comes from the upload form."""
+    command = f"convert {UPLOAD_DIR}/{upload_name} -resize 128x128 {THUMB_DIR}/{upload_name}"
+    subprocess.run(command, shell=True, check=True)  # nosec B602

truth.text: The file name from the upload form goes into a shell command, and the nosec comment hides the scanner rule that would report it, so a name with shell syntax runs commands. The fix is to pass an argument list without shell=True and to drop the suppression.
